reviews.text: Yes, Creed II is a boxing film. Yes, it is a story that we have seen played out at least seven previous times. But there is so much more under the surface, and that is where Creed II shines.
reviews.author: Max Greene

reviews.text: Watching the characters struggle to manage the consequences of the past with the responsibilities of the future is both interesting and dramatic.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: In conclusion, Creed II is a solid film with a convincing performance of  Michael B. Jordan who asserts himself in the character. This sequel is what the fans expected, but it must be admitted that it provides few innovative elements.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: This film is the return of a Ford Mustang and a grudge match between Adonis Creed with the son of the man who killed his father, Viktor Drago, is predictable and you wonder if these two would be in the same division.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: ...essentially a remake of Rocky IV.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The movie adheres to every narrative beat predictably, including a climactic bout that proves deflated and visually uninspired.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Creed II is an overall blast. With well-defined characters, thrilling action, and stunning cinematography, audiences will be treated to a dramatically compelling and fun time in the theater.
reviews.author: Swara Salih

reviews.text: Perhaps the greatest accomplishment of “Creed II” is that you don’t feel the absence of Ryan Coogler. That’s not a knock on Coogler, but high praise for Caple, Jr.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Episode 20: When Jeff Tried To Save The World / Creed II / The Ballad of Buster Scruggs / The World Is Yours / Burning
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Beyond all the trimmings of its Rocky rematch, the film packs a surprisingly powerful punch and offers a layered story about the power we give the past.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: The magnetism of Michael B. Jordan and the history of the various characters keep the film from ever going underwater, making it plausible for this version of the franchise to become a trilogy in the near future.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: This feels like Stallone handing over the gloves to Jordan and they're going onto capable hands.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Reverberates with echoes of Rockys past but transcends being an exercise in déjà vu by amping up the emotional content to TKO levels. Neither a rehash nor completely original work it's simply another puzzle piece in the feel good Rocky saga.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Everything about the film happens like clockwork; there's not a single moment that isn't entirely anticipated.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: "Creed II" not only does the franchise justice, it's further proof of Stallone's lasting creation. I predict at least one more "Creed," then possibly a "Million Dollar Baby" style spinoff series with Adonis' daughter Amara to keep the franchise running.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: A highly entertaining, very emotionally satisfying second round that lands most of its punches, proving to be a sequel that is bound to get audiences pumped.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: If the film had been called Drago, it could have taken a more original, nuanced look at busting open the bad guy mythology and rising above a generically entertaining structure.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: This could be a fascinating look at the franchise's own cyclicality, but Stallone and Taylor don't inject much of any self-awareness in their script. They rely on formula.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Creed II, like the second Rocky film, is a comeback story. It's the tale of a rematch. Unfortunately for the audience, the trajectory of Creed II so closely resembles Rocky II that the film becomes painfully predictable.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Not quite living up to its predecessor, the Rocky hardcore fan base will still get a major kick at this nostalgic fight back. More Rocky 7 than Creed 2, the first half missed the brilliance of Coogler, but it came back fighting in the second half.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: It is a routine sequel weighed down by the most hackneyed components of the genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Creed II works best as a story about fathers and sons, and the legacies we are either blessed or cursed with at birth.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Creed II is hit and miss, but it's a mostly worthy successor to a film so strong, it would almost be impossible to match. Due largely to a cast that brings more to the film than the screenplay can sustain, the movie delivers in most of the right places.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Since it has borrowed from its parent franchise, Creed II's plot devices are pure sports movie pedigree, but, like its predecessor, the direction and performances raise it to a higher level.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: reed 2 film doesn't reach the dizzying heights of the original but is still a quasi-satisfying chapter in the Rocky franchise.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: Scripted by Stallone and Juel Taylor, Creed II deserves a cheer.
reviews.author: Rhodé Marshall

reviews.text: Stallone has never been one to phone it in, and his script, as silly as it can be, is vintage Rocky. The performances are fantastic as well.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Battle fatigue sets in roughly halfway through this eighth installment of Sylvester Stallone's Rocky franchise.
reviews.author: Andrea Gronvall

reviews.text: Overall, Michael B. Jordan knocks it out of the park (or the ring?) again, providing a strong emotional backbone to the movie.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: I almost found myself rooting for Viktor Drago to win the final fight, not because of any anti-American sentiment, but because it's always fun to see the actual underdog win.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: Creed II is like the best parts of Rocky II-V hot glued together.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Much like the Rocky Sequels, this movie is a good movie, it pulls you in and you really do care about Adonis, Bianca, and Rocky and all those who surround them, as well as their antagonists.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: A tale as old as time, yet Creed II feels fresher than ever
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: Overall, Creed II falls short of its predecessor - but that doesn't stop Michael B. Jordan owning the screen.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: It takes a comparatively straight-forward sequel and turns into something special.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: [Steven] Caple knows what a Rocky fan expects. The scripted violence inside the ring is still exciting even after we think we've seen it all before
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Only time will tell if the Creed series will last as long as the Rocky films that preceded it, but thus far, they've helped launch careers for two young and talented black filmmakers.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: There is no fresh thought in Creed II. But it is a movie in the Rocky Universe that will fetch it box office numbers.
reviews.author: Rucha Sharma

reviews.text: Jordan is one of Hollywood's hot, young actors and it's easy to see why here. We see his inner struggle and feel his pain right along with him.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Boxer Adonis Creed is at the apex of his game as world heavyweight champion. His world is looking mighty fine-although, naturally, not for long.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Watching Michael B. Jordan and Tessa Thompson clawing and biting their way through the wretched melodrama they are bound and gagged by is as frustrating as imagining what Creed II could have been in the hands of Ryan Coogler and his team.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Creed II might tell a familiar story, but thanks to great fight scenes and a dynamite cast bringing life to great characters it turns into a great movie overall.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: That rare sequel that holds its own both in comparison to its predecessor and on its own accord.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Creed II has thunderous heart. It may dip into Hallmark card territory from time to time, but the performances are electric and the words of wisdom it passes along are applicable to anyone's life.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Not as good as its predecessor (because it knows it doesn't need to be), but Creed II is still a knockout.
reviews.author: Chase Whale

reviews.text: Like Rocky Balboa and Adonis Creed, Creed II takes the hits and keeps on standing.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: While [it] isn't great, it's a solid entry in the "Rocky" anthology with pros thankfully outweighing the cons.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: It's less personal, and basically consists of a sturdy mix of fight scenes and soap opera, but it wraps its bulging arms and soft heart around you in a comfortable, squeezing hug.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Full of moments that will have franchise fans watching through teary eyes at the first sniff of an emotional beat or fist-pumping anthem.
reviews.author: Andrew Pollard

reviews.text: A sequel that is almost at the same level as the first film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Despite its predictability, Creed II still manages to feel like an epic. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Overall, the film follows what is almost a formulaic narrative, but this is not a shortcoming in light of the poignant storytelling.
reviews.author: Min-sik Yoon

reviews.text: Creed II has its shortcomings and pales in comparison to its predecessor. It's just like how the sequels to Rocky fared. But Caple Jr. crafts a second part that entertains more than it disappoints.
reviews.author: Deborah Cornelious

reviews.text: [Tessa Thompson] gives the film a sort of density that neither Michael B. Jordan nor Stallone himself managed to maintain. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aarón Rodríguez Serrano

reviews.text: Creed II is okay -- the kind of movie you could easily watch on cable without feeling as if you had totally wasted your time -- but it is by no means a knockout.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: It might be full of contradictions, but Creed II is passionate and confident enough to win you over anyway.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: Completely predictable; full of stand-up-and-cheer moments, as well as references to previous films of the saga. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: I was really hoping this would be the movie where he leaves the "Rocky nest" and spreads his wings and fly, but I suppose we'd have to wait and see in another potential sequel.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: The director integrates every iconic element... For fans of the saga, it's the perfect film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: Good thing Creed II is very aware of what audiences came here for, because the movie not only delivers, it makes its cliches feel like they matter.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Heft and depth go far in this eighth franchise instalment. In the ring and on the screen, you can't connect without both.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: The story enraptures you with its simplicity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: There is an accumulation of melodramatic components that weaken the effect of the style. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Francisco Marinero

reviews.text: Creed II spins a beautiful, engaging yarn about a damaged egotist that held me rapt despite myself.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: One of the most pleasant surprises of the film is the work of Dolph Lundgren and Florian Munteanu as Ivan and Viktor Drago, respectively. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: The film appeals in a very direct and unequivocal way, without fuss, with simple but very effective mechanisms. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Marañón

reviews.text: An appropriate continuation of the Creed legacy
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: It works like a good entry in the Rocky saga. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: Thanks to the commitment of the returning cast, the sincere faithfulness to the franchise, its blunt-force dramatic approach and the intense boxing scenes, Creed 2 is a great sequel that's worth running out to watch.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: It's not particularly innovative, but it has a narrative built with pure rigor, nobility and perseverance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Creed II commits almost the same mistakes as Rocky II. Repeat, reiterate schemes, and the fights have neither the spectacle nor the composition that director Ryan Coogler... had achieved in Creed (2015). [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The film has a great ability to alternate a theme with another montage, evading the lower jabs that could make one feel more tragic. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: If Creed II ends up being the definitive end for these characters, it would be the most emotional and captivating film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Iván Belmont

reviews.text: A step down in many ways from its predecessor, Creed II  is still a solid and worthy sequel.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: [T]he film explores well enough how much of the past shapes who we become, and with Jordan, Thompson, and Stallone, it creates an endearing onscreen family.
reviews.author: Valerie Kalfrin

reviews.text: Close to an XL for me. It's a sequel that uses a rehash of storylines and characters that still actually held up.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: This movie could have easily fallen apart, but even with Stallone contributing to the writing, Steven Caple Jr. hit a home run with this.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: An emotional rematch - although a bit worn - in which the combat keeps you at the edge of your seat. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mabel Salinas

reviews.text: Creed II is neither as assured nor as rousing as its predecessor, but it has a secret weapon up its boxing gloves, and that is to embrace the daftest elements of the series while simultaneously finding the heart that drives every good Rocky film.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: A blandly predictable sports movie given some kind of disreputable interest by inserting itself into the mythology of an iconic, if not particularly high-quality franchise.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The weakest of all the Rocky/Creed movies...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Enjoyable in fits and starts.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Creed II fits the mold of every Rocky sequel-competent, entertaining, and a little passionless
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: It uses a well-worn formula to create a fresh, invigorating experience.
reviews.author: Greg Maki

reviews.text: Lacks some of the (sorry) punch of its predecessor but Creed II still shines on the strength of Michael B. Jordan.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: What plays on screen is a caricature of the franchise, a film so loathe to have its own identity that it forgets everything that made previous installments must-see cinema.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: The film is hard to dislike because of the two strong performances from its leading men.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: CREED II find a legacy through making mistakes. It's messy, and we don't always bring out the best parts of ourselves. The trick is to breathe, listen, open up.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Playing like the greatest hits of every Rocky sequel to date, Creed II is bigger and its hits thud harder, but it misses the emotional focus and finesse of its predecessor.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: The boxing sequences are brutal, no matter how much people want to turn boxing into a metaphor for inner growth and building character. The message is that family matters above all.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: What ensues is enjoyably rooted in sentiment, genre stereotype and Rocky mythology, but does drag a little between the brutal but brilliantly staged fight scenes.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Feeling to have less energy than the preceding film, it's still an enjoyable and competently made follow-up ... and a fitting swan-song for the character of Rocky Balboa.
reviews.author: Colby Bryant

reviews.text: It's a letdown for a good movie that had all the makings of greatness, but, ultimately, is let down by an overly predictable narrative.
reviews.author: Damian Levy

reviews.text: The dramatic pull of Adonis fighting the son of his father's killer is obvious but riveting all the same, made even more engrossing by the shadow of Rocky Balboa.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: It's just another Rocky sequel, and that sucks.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: It is strange to say this, but the thing that carries the biggest sting here - especially in the scenes when Stallone's Rocky, aware that he is in his life's twilight, muses about roads not taken - is not the boxing, but the bonding.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: This follow-up isn't as good as the original, but it has enough fight left in it to go the distance and end up winning over the scoring judges. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: But despite its own individual merits, this year's sequel, Creed II, fails to quite live up to the potential of its predecessor, and Coogler himself seems to be the essential missing ingredient.
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: The chemistry between the cast members - whether it's between Stallone and Jordan or Thompson and Jordan - makes the film all the more believable.
reviews.author: Masego Panyane

reviews.text: There's... so much to enjoy in Creed II.
reviews.author: Brooke Obie

reviews.text: Gripping and poignant, Creed II marks the humble passing of the mantle. Just need Mr. T's son for next time.
reviews.author: Cameron Frew

reviews.text: Creed II does beat you over the head with its sentimentalism - too much text instead of subtext. But it's generally effective,
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: ...the same thumping and grinding sports movie clichés and oodles of heavy-duty macho soul-baring.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: This sequel answers the bell and then some, giving us something that, while not quite a bout for the ages, turns out to be a hell of a fight.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The fight choreography is on point and the sound editing of punches makes it feel like you are the one who has been hit.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: The film never quite finds a consistent tone but it never stops being entertaining either.
reviews.author: Sarah Cullen

reviews.text: A solid film that pulls you in in the way these films do, but if you come in knowing that, you let the path take you.
reviews.author: Aisha Jordan

reviews.text: Ultimately though, Creed II is as much a male weepie or old-school melodrama as it is a boxing movie, and this is actually where it succeeds best.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: If this is indeed Rocky's last time ringside, it's a solid if predictable farewell to one of American cinema's most enduring characters.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: While Creed II does not reach the fantastic heights of Creed, it still puts up plenty of fight to prove itself worthy.
reviews.author: Jake Tropila

reviews.text: ... refreshingly less concerned with trite triumphs than it is with fractured men forced to confront who they perceive themselves to be or aspire to be vs. who they are - and the fight to reconcile that.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: Of course Creed II is familiar ground. But it honours the genre and still has enough vitality to make us feel the thrill again.
reviews.author: Anupama Chopra

reviews.text: New director Steven Caple Jr (Emmett Till) keeps the film at a simmer in between the bouts and his cast are uniformly terrific.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The fact that Creed II is so predictable takes nothing away from the excitement. The scenes in the ring are superbly shot and slickly edited, the thud of each blow enough to send you reeling back into the cinema seat.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: Steven Caple Jr's film is watchable enough if you're a fan of its traditions, but Jordan is too sleek and handsome for his suffering to be as glorious as Sylvester Stallone's agonies in days gone by.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: Just as Adonis Creed is a worthy of the Apollo Creed legacy, Creed II is another deserving addition to the Rocky canon.
reviews.author: Deirdre Crimmins

reviews.text: It's an effective sequel to two very different movies grown from the same cinematic DNA.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: There are a lot of great things about CREED II. It's a meditation on the fathers that never showed up, those too lost in their own success to truly be present, those too deep in their own shame to provide comfort. It is not exactly new but still well done
reviews.author: Tim Stevens

reviews.text: Creed II is almost a match for its predecessor in most respects, and in one its superior.
reviews.author: Matthew Norman

reviews.text: Jordan is the best thing about the film; vulnerable mouth and defiant, boyish attitude voice ("I'm dangerous!" he insists, voice cracking) telegraphing insecurity and impostor syndrome that feels lived in.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Doesn't hit the heights of its predecessor, but it's still an effective, hard-hitting story that honours what came before and allows Jordan the chance to shine again.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Director Steven Caple Jr. takes over from Ryan Coogler to deliver a worthy follow-up that lands heavy blows where it counts and in a few places that are unexpected.
reviews.author: Ross Miller

reviews.text: There are those for whom Rocky IV is the preferred chapter in the original series. Creed II is a gift to us.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: You can feel the punches being landed... because you care about the characters.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: A pensive, tough-minded, extremely well-directed drama that refuses to take easy options or cop outs.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The film is slickly shot. And the fight scenes are nicely choreographed. You feel the pain of the boxers as they slug it out.
reviews.author: Devesh Sharma

reviews.text: More than anything, it deserves kudos for managing to make Rocky IV relevant and impactful again, rather than just using it to take easy pot shots at Cold War jingoism.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: [Director Steven Caple Jr.] acquits himself well and delivers the formula with confidence. But the sequel can't deliver the same energetic freshness of Creed.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Perfectly serviceable as both a boxing movie and a Rocky movie, but it's missing that extra gear that the first Creed had (Philadelphia Weekly)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: In spite of the clumsy storyline and more pedestrian approach overall, the shock of Creed II is that it all still works so well.
reviews.author: Garth Franklin

reviews.text: I don't think I have sat before a boxing film where the punches felt harder, even 10 rows back from the screen.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Ryan Coogler, having gone on to bigger and bigger things, steps aside and lets relative newcomer Steven Caple, Jr. do the job of mixing the beats of Rocky III and Rocky IV into a smooth groove for the son of Apollo Creed (Michael B. Jordan).
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: As the eighth instalment in an ancient boxing franchise, Creed II should not be this good. Yet at times it is flat-out thrilling.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: [Creed II] holds fast to the Rocky traditions and, though rather predictable, is utterly irresistible from the start.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Can't quite manage to continue the first film's smart, unsentimental examination of male emotion and men's relationships. At best achieves a draw with a genre path that is already extremely well worn.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Hugely enjoyable, with some terrific performances and a keen eye on the continuing evolution of the series, while maintaining the heart of the original.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: If Creed was almost as good as Rocky, Creed II is almost as good as Creed.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Far from the knock-out punch of the first film,Creed II still makes an impact.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: I bloody LOVED it. It hit every beat, tugged every string and left me feeling 12 again.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: The fight scenes are decent, Stallone's still appealing, and when Bill Conti's original theme kicks in, it's impossible to resist. But please, no more.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: When a film is as unashamedly formulaic as Creed II, the formula had better be a good one. Fortunately, it is.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Settle in for an exceedingly average story, a total lack of thrills, and far too little of Sylvester Stallone.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: The movie does offer one genuine surprise: the Drago family drama actually eclipses anything going on with the Creeds or Balboas.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Creed II ramps up the nostalgia in a story that's as much a family drama as a boxing movie.
reviews.author: Tom Glasson

reviews.text: Sadly, the first Creed's director, Ryan Coogler, didn't stick around for a sequel and it shows. But this is still a solid, earnestly acted effort.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: The Rocky franchise is nothing if not redundant, or rather, full of reverberations, past stories just waiting to be mined by some later sequel. Creed II doesn't quite make a meal of the opportunity.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: How do you top a film that managed to reignite a seemingly extinct franchise? Going by Creed II, the answer is you can't, but you should sure as hell try.
reviews.author: Benjamin Rabinovich

reviews.text: Whatever you think about Rocky IV, it is inarguably a mid-1980s time capsule. Creed II isn't a time capsule, but it should get buried.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Creed II is by no means a bad film, but like the first sequel to the original 1976 Rocky it settles for a box-ticking template that seems reluctant to bring any tangible forward momentum to the franchise.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

reviews.text: It's a sturdy second round after a cracking first one.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: 42 years since the original 'Rocky' and, even if he's taken a backseat for new blood, Stallone is the still the MVP of this franchise.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Creed II, the sequel to 2015's excellent Creed and the eighth overall entry in the Rocky saga, lives up to the legend, which is saying something, because, well, did you read the first part of this sentence?
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: You see it coming. The same goes for much of the dialogue. Even so, this is an enjoyable and rousing affair that wins you over by the sheer process of attrition.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: While Creed II isn't quite as fresh or fleet of foot as its predecessor, it still lands telling blows in all the right places, and ends with its arms held aloft in triumph.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: An entertaining next chapter that manages to both stand on its own and serve as fun nostalgia for one of the Rocky franchise's most iconic villains.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Eight movies in, and you'd think there'd be some better, fleshed-out characters populating this universe.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Cheerfully ludicrous.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: This movie, like some of the other movies in the Rocky series is about heart. In Rocky, the boxer's power comes from his heart, and from the people he loves. That theme is repeated here very effectively.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Creed II misses a major opportunity to tell a great story about fathers and sons.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: If you were delivering a lecture on how to extract the most value from a worn formula then you could do worse than direct your audience to the latest film in the Rocky cycle.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Totally satisfying sequel, packing a powerful wallop...
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: It is a solid movie that further cements Jordan as a star, and that's mostly because of how he portrays Donnie's personal development.
reviews.author: Brandon Katz

reviews.text: Creed 2 doesn't pack as big of an emotional punch as its predecessor, but I just can't get enough of these characters. The Rocky nostalgia hasn't worn off yet, and this film proves that it won't any time soon.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: Sometimes, a sports movie is just a sports movie, and Creed II is an entertaining movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Though it lacks the knockout blow of Ryan Coogler's first, unable to live up to the genuine surprise of a great series spin-off, it's still an entertaining contender.
reviews.author: Adam Fresco

reviews.text: The film simmers before it explodes, and it often, it maintains the slow burn for a moment too long in the quieter moments between family members. But when Caple really lets "Creed II" run wild, it's breathtaking.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: The stakes are there, but what this movie did well was it made you sympathetic to the Drago family...There's more weight to it now.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: This episode in this extended tale of fighting men and the warrior creed demos father-son dynamics, and especially between Ivan and Viktor Drago -- forgiveness and compassion. These are the building blocks of nontoxic masculinity.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: This new entry plays things just above safe, being a crazy good crowd pleaser that is both level-headed and daring, but within set limits.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: Doesn't punch nearly as hard without Coogler in its corner.
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: What saves it is Michael B. Jordon. Sure, the first thing you notice is the power, the arm cocked, ready to fire. But his real strength is his openness...the way he allows himself to be emotionally vulnerable.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: The way disability gets used as a plot device to further Adonis' narrative feels mishandled.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: Despite a predictable script and workmanlike execution behind the camera, the cast elevates the material with their performances to craft another entertaining entry into the Rocky saga
reviews.author: Sam Stone

reviews.text: Creed II is gonna to be a winner for any fan of the Rocky franchise, but it's also going to be a win you over if you're not. At its core, it's a family movie that asks some very deep questions...
reviews.author: Dante James

reviews.text: The ineffective emotional stakes, watered-down drama, and threadbare relational conflicts make Creed 2 exceedingly impersonal.
reviews.author: Tre Johnson

reviews.text: This is a return to that punch-drunk Rocky movie vibe, with obvious heroes and villains and internal conflicts that are vivid but never go very deep.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It's not entirely without its merits -- as much as seems rote, it's still a far cry from '80s-style cartoon buffoonery -- but just as quickly as Creed sprung up out of nowhere, this revised series already feels more than a little played out.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Creed II is not nearly as rousing, heartbreaking, and life affirming as the original. However, on it's own terms, it's an enjoyable sequel that nimbly brings Adonis into the fold of the original films.
reviews.author: Michael Fairbanks

reviews.text: Creed II, along with the entire Creed spinoff, has managed to be an incredible revival of a beloved franchise, a black movie that is proud of its blackness, and also a good romance.
reviews.author: Princess Weekes

reviews.text: One of the overarching themes of Creed II is stepping out of the shadow of the greatness that came before you. This is a lesson the Creed franchise needs to learn. You can only get so much mileage using the Rocky films as a springboard.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: A spiritual sequel to Rocky IV released in the midst of a new Cold War and it turns out to be completely apolitical? What a disappointment.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Have the "Creed" movies learned nothing from the "Rocky" series? Sequels aren't always the answer.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: This flashy sequel is an entertaining entry that fits into the Rocky franchise like it's a part of the family.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: The whole thing just ... works.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: An entertaining and satisfying sequel that respects the past while it sets up its own future. Michael B. Jordan is a beast here. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: It's a step down from its predecessor, but hey, aren't we all? It works well enough as yet another Rocky sequel.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: More like a sequel to Rocky IV than to the superior Creed, but Stallone (who also co-wrote the script) and Michael B. Jordan know exactly how to deliver the goods so the audience will be happy with this.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Director Steven Caple Jr. ("The Land") inherits the thankless task of following in the footsteps of talented "Creed" helmer Ryan Coogler, but no one could have rescued a ho-hum script credited to six writers, including Coogler and Stallone.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: This one is as bloated as an overweight boxer. The best reason to love anything from the Rocky series is Sylvester Stallone's Rocky & even Stallone isn't that likable here.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Not only a superb follow-up to the breakout 2015 hit, but it's a worthy continuation of Rocky IV. There's not a lot of films that could so skillfully expand on two films.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: There was a great movie in "Creed II," one that peeked out every now and then beneath the suffocating blanket of clichés.
reviews.author: Matthew Rozsa

reviews.text: The actors are all on point, the storytelling through action is brutal, crisp and satisfying and whichever of the two credited screenwriters came up with Adonis' ring-entrance gimmick should get a special Oscar just for that note.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: CREED II is your best case scenario. It lives up to the original and also stands on its own two feet, boding well for CREED III, IV and beyond
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Surprisingly touching treatment of villains makes up for rote boxing action.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: It's a miracle that after eight films in the franchise, the formula can still pull the emotional punches regarding: fathers, redemption, loneliness, family - and somehow remain fresh.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: ... its understanding of the franchise's history is evident and a significant contributor to creating a movie that long-time fans will enjoy.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: ...visceral sports action and heart-squeezing emotional drama.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: If the results aren't as artful as those by Creed director Ryan Coogler (Steven Caple Jr. steps in), they still feel earned.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: Where Caple's direction is truly mastered is in his active command of his actors, most notably Michael B. Jordan and Tessa Thompson. Strap in, because "Creed II" is a wild, great time at the movies.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: Creed II should be seen as a highlight of the series, easily becoming one of the best sequels in franchise history... Jordan shines again and again.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Under the less-inspired direction of Steven Caple Jr., Creed II feels like a compilation of greatest Rocky scenes climaxed by a final match so ludicrously cliched that viewers groaned during a Monday screening...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Even though we've seen this movie before (and more than once), there's a strong beating heart to this franchise.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Rocky movies are a genre within a genre, and their audiences expect or even demand they be 95 percent predictable. So when they're even ten percent surprising - a generous estimate of Creed II's novelty quotient - it feels like a win.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: For a film about fathers and sons, Creed II doesn't much evolve the portrait of fatherhood. ... [but it] has some relevant things to say about male fragility.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Creed II is a really enjoyable film and takes its characters to such great places that I have no desire to see more.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Creed II isn't as good as the first installment, but it's no disgrace, either. Credit the cast for keeping familiar characters alive -- if a little bruised.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Finds a way to rehash without losing heart, also doing something compelling with a potentially ridiculous plot.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Despite its lack of flair and depth in terms of both storytelling and filmmaking, Creed II does absolutely succeed in being an entertaining boxing movie.
reviews.author: Matt Miller

reviews.text: From the ding of the first bell to the echo of the last, Creed II is ... a stirring drama that utilizes every inch of emotional real estate to enormous effect.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: It may struggle in the other departments, but Creed II is a really satisfying Rocky movie. It's just that I think I prefer the Creed movies now.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan and Sylvester Stallone again provide a potent one-two combo, in a movie filled with nostalgic callbacks that make the most of the franchise's durable formula.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Audiences have now invested decades in this ringside soap opera and they want to see where it goes, despite everything else. And, when all is said and done, the fight scenes are actually quite good.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The fact it all works as well as it does is a testament to how rich the performances are as well as the kinetically captivating efficiency of Caple's direction.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The "Rocky" formula is good enough that these films could probably go on forever, but now that the Drago story is out of the way, Stallone should really pass the torch and give Adonis Creed a movie of his own.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: If what you seek is a good "Rocky" movie then "Creed II" delivers the goods.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: One reason Creed II manages to avoid totally losing itself in Rocky lore is simple: It's still rooted in a movie that took its characters and their emotional complexities seriously.
reviews.author: Emily St. James

reviews.text: Despite repeating the same beats as most Rocky films, the film emulates the fighting spirit of Rocky Balboa and manages to triumph. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: "Creed II" doesn't pack the same punch, either emotionally or in the ring, but as with seven "Rocky" movies before it, longtime fans will still be cheering by the end of this sequel.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: It's not quite ROCKY II, but then it's not ROCKY III, either.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: A generation later, the partial sequel, partial reboot of the great boxing franchise is falling neatly in line with its legacy.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: There is more pleasure in watching Rocky Balboa call the Philly DPW about a broken street light than in the film's climactic fight.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The solid sequel I wanted Creed II to be.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: The sequel isn't in the same lofty space as the first "Creed," but it's a sure crowd-pleaser with some added emotional punch.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: "Creed II" goes the distance, but it lacks the knockout punch of its 2015 and 1985 predecessors.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Gone are the little moments of humanity that punched us in the gut when the suspense of victory was absent. Gone are the pangs of loss, guilt, and regret with real consequences.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: For a film whose hero's purpose is to uppercut the expectations embroiled in his name, Creed II ironically and regrettably takes refuge in its franchise's beaten down, yet irresistibly feel-good formula.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: While the film falls short of delivering a knockout punch, Creed II is able to go the distance thanks to excellent boxing sequences and the return of Ivan Drago.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Maybe a younger generation needs this update, but fans schooled in the franchise history will consider it all a retread, with only a new boxer at the film's center.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Like the iconic Rocky statue itself, the film and its series are triumphant, immovable and gleaming in bronzed defiance.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Almost single-handedly, Michael B. Jordan takes this film the distance. In gestures, attitude and a wide range of expressions, he makes Adonis far more complex than the film itself.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: The Rocky formula matters more than the characters in it.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: If this year's soft reboot of "Halloween" bridged old and new fans to an iconic horror franchise, "Creed II" does the same for devotees of the "Rocky" series.
reviews.author: Garrett Mitchell

reviews.text: Keep one's expectations low. If you can do that, then Creed II delivers well beyond them.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: You'll cheer, no doubt. Creed II still disappoints, especially in one critical reunion we didn't know we needed to see.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: "Creed II" is a respectable if not revelatory sequel to the sequel, even if it lacks its predecessor's grace and narrative texture.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Creed II is a perfectly OK sequel. There's some comfort to be found in the predictability of its beats. But only at the end does it muster any real vitality.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: At its best moments, "Creed II" manages a feat nearly as striking as anything that Michael B. Jordan's Rocky Balboa protégé pulls off in the boxing ring: It doesn't play all that much like a sequel.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: Pretty much the movie everyone was afraid "Creed" was going to be.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It's always fun to decry a formulaic movie - except when the formula actually works.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Caple doesn't always connect, but he does have Sylvester Stallone and Michael B. Jordan packing a one-two punch as Rocky Balboa and Adonis Creed.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: It feels more like 'Rocky VII' than 'Creed II,' recycling the old franchise tropes rather than reimagining them in the way its predecessor did.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: This surprisingly effective second chapter proves that Adonis Creed still has something left in the tank.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Creed II lacks the panache of the original installment but has enough emotion and inspiration to find itself a perfect fit for the Rocky franchise
reviews.author: Kristen Lopez

reviews.text: These don't need to be directed by auteurs to succeed, and Cable delivers what he needs to without getting in the film's way.
reviews.author: Evan Saathoff

reviews.text: The whole of the film, directed by Steven Caple Jr., is a subtle progression away from the past.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: By playing things too safe, it loses the power and spontaneity that gave Creed its energy and drive.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Admirably carries Adonis Creed and Rocky Balboa's stories forward while somehow managing to wring real stakes and real drama from the most comically over-the-top installment in the Rocky saga's entire four-decade arsenal.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: Creed 2 is the movie we were afraid the first, far superior Creed was going to be.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: The latest installment in the seemingly endless Rocky franchise offers nothing new but still may appeal to fans of the genre.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: Soaked in pugilistic blood, fervent sweat, and warranted tears, Creed II is comfortably ingrained big screen entertainment.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Stallone's lovably tough Rocky is as solid as ever, and Jordan and Thompson make a ferocious couple.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The fight scenes are appropriately intense and amazingly choreographed, and the performances are all solid, making it an overall enjoyable experience. Still, I wonder what it would have been like had if Creed II had a bit more heart.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: Creed 2 is a commendable chapter in the franchise, thriving from a strong commitment to character, mostly thanks to Stallone's reverence to his own legacy and the new one being created for Jordan.
reviews.author: Michael Roffman

reviews.text: Although "Creed 2" doesn't have the same rousing magic as the last chapter, it offers intriguing parallel plots of fathers and sons trying to find redemption after loss.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: So, sure, Creed II has elements of boxing to it, but the heart of the story is with these men dealing with the emotions of fatherhood, opening up, and owning their past mistakes to move on with their futures.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: Merely adopting a formula is easy - that happens all too often. Investing in a formula, making it breathe - that's the challenge, and "Creed II" meets it.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: "Creed II" deftly pulls together threads from all of the "Rocky" movies, underscoring that it's time to acknowledge that Sylvester Stallone's Rocky Balboa is one of the greatest of all Hollywood characters.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Strong performances combined with the sturdy, albeit measured direction by Steven Caple Jr., manage to ensure that although Creed II often comes across as a guilty pleasure, there's no shame in enjoying it for nostalgic reasons.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: There is nothing wrong with Creed II other than the fact that it isn't Creed.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: Oh, so what if it isn't the knockout the original Creed was? This one still lands its punches, even if a little more softly.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: "Creed II" steps inside the ropes under the heavy weight of expectations, is not as nimble and has put on some pounds around the middle. Yet while the film doesn't get heads ringing like the first one, it's still able to go the distance.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: "Creed II" is a terrific movie, a boxing picture full of inspired sweetness and shrewd science that honors the cherished traditions of the genre while feeling like something new and exciting in the world.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Creed II refuses to go toe-to-toe with anything vaguely political, essentially ignoring any and all of the headlines of the past two years in what can only be described as an exhausting display of political aloofness.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Creed II is like spending time at McDonald's among friends. It's satisfying and warm, but not something you want to be doing all the time.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: ...as a boxing movie, this is pretty solid, the equivalent of a song you've heard 100 times being covered by a new artist. But Creed felt like a new song; Creed II feels like a decent cover of that new song.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: The biggest problem with Creed II is that the 8th installment of the Rocky franchise...plays it safe.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Thompson gives a performance just as sensitive and strong-willed as her last, and her chemistry with Jordan is even greater this time. Jordan continues to impress, navigating the emotional territory of the movie better than Stallone ever did.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Sheer entertainment value covers up the scars from a recognizable story that has been beaten to a bloody pulp
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Creed II may not advance Adonis' story, but it's still a good Rocky film nonetheless.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Caple gives us well drawn characters we're invested in all while dealing with the cliché boxing tropes with restraint and maintaining the gritty tone Coogler established in the original.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Strong sequel has boxing violence, some language.
reviews.author: Michael Ordoña

reviews.text: Creed II has compelling drama hitting you from all sides.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Dolph Lundgren in close-up, in various moods of granite determination and unexpected emotional thawing, qualifies as this sequel's most legit surprise.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Go in expecting greatness, and you're likely to be disappointed. Go in expecting a Rocky sequel, and you'll get a surprisingly effective one.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Creed II does have a pulse, even if you know almost everything that's going to happen a couple of breaths before it does.
reviews.author: Alan Scherstuhl

reviews.text: Creed II falls victim to the sins of sequelitis-it's bigger, louder and more grandiose than its predecessor-yet manages to right itself by not losing focus on the humanity of its central characters.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: A surprise-free movie can be a satisfying one, if the grace notes are played with care. They are in Creed II.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Creed II is a testament to Stallone's ability to re-write this same movie over and over again and make it work endlessly for audiences old and new.
reviews.author: Michael Heaton

reviews.text: What easily could have tarnished what's come before instead movingly builds on it. This is one of the ten best films of 2018, unlikely as that may seem.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: A solid, emotionally rich sequel that builds upon the Creed legacy.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Creed II is absent of both the topically political atmosphere of Rocky IV and the bravura action of Ryan Coogler's Creed.
reviews.author: Sam C. Mac

reviews.text: For Creed II to do a Creed style dramatic exploration of the aftermath of pure '80s cheese is a bold move, and a successful one.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: I loved this movie, for so many different reasons...it could have gone so wrong, so cheesy, but instead it turned into something that's a franchise.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: A very capable sequel to a very popular movie.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: Creed II does not give us anything but another, slightly superior Rocky sequel. It wins on points. Just don't expect a knockout.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: It's a familiar sequel in which audiences will be able to anticipate every single narrative punch.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: Creed II is to Creed what the Rocky sequels are to the original: a more generic, less textured take on familiar boxing movie tropes. The difference, it seems, is Coogler.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Creed II is much like the annoying boxing match announcer that infects most of the movie: trying too hard to sound exciting while not telling you anything new or interesting
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: A knockout sequel that packs the same impacting punch as its predecessor.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: This sequel accomplishes its modest goals, and yet what's frustrating about this latest chapter in the Adonis Creed saga is that, whatever ambitions it might have, the primary objective is to fashion a familiar Rocky adventure.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: The rift is part of the rather transparent and predictable structure of Creed II, which feels more like an indifferent Rocky sequel than a movie with the reinvented dynamism of Creed.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Creed II is exactly what you want from a Rocky/Creed film: it's engaging, emotional, gripping, and entertaining, pushing the characters forward in all the right ways.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: I love watching the relationship between Ivan and Victor as they try to restore their families names.
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams

reviews.text: It's a state of emotional stymieing that Jordan pulls off well, particularly in light of a heavy-handed script.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: The only thing driving the story forward is the strength of Michael B. Jordan, Tessa Thompson, and Sylvester Stallone's performances, but they're nearly lost in a sea of missed opportunities.
reviews.author: Tom Jorgensen

reviews.text: Can't live up to the legacy even of the previous Creed movie, let alone any of the Rocky movies, when it relies so heavily on every predictable boxing cliché imaginable.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: It's depressing that after Creed's success, Creed II feels like it's just a step above a straight-to-video knockoff, designed to get a little more from the first movie's audience but not to increase it.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: Nothing here has been freshly thought out, nor is there a drop of surprise as to the story's trajectory, forcing the viewer to tolerate conventional emotional beats and stale plot contrivances.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Sometimes the movie feels torn between spare evocations of a boxer's life and crowd-pleasing evocations of past movies. But more often than not, Caple splits the difference with aplomb.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: It's not quite as smart as Creed, or quite as beautiful, and it doesn't have as much depth or nuance or texture. But it's got enough to deliver something satisfying and sweet.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: The Land director Steven J. Caple Jr. has made a rousing tale about fathers and sons, guilt and redemption, loneliness and family - just the sort of big, sledgehammer-subtle themes that have always propelled the series.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: "Creed II" elevates the literal and metaphorical challenges of following up improbable success to something meaningful and eventually transcendent of the formulas that it relies upon.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: "Creed II" may not be the freshest entry in the franchise, but it's a solid sports drama that makes the most of its soulful young star, Michael B. Jordan.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: We know what to expect from these stories, but both "Creed" and its sequel invite us to forget - so we can rediscover the thrill all over again.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Caple orchestrates a worthy sequel that still has those needed references to the "Rocky" franchise the fans crave, but makes a point to build up Adonis' own story.
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: Jordan remains a model of dimensional ferocity, laced with the right vulnerability.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: For a movie that features a dramatic fight between people with the last name Creed and Drago, it's strangely sad and reflective.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Very much a Rocky sequel.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Creed II is serviceable and enjoyable even if one can see the punches coming from a mile away.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: "Creed II" has been made with heart and skill, and Jordan invests each moment with such fierce conviction that he makes it all seem like it matters.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Elevated by a central trio of winning performances and a director who provides equal weight to drama in and out of the ring, Creed II deserves to be cheered.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: The rare sequel that doesn't wind up feeling like the same old mistake.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

synopsis: In 1985, Russian boxer Ivan Drago killed former U.S. champion Apollo Creed in a tragic match that stunned the world. Against the wishes of trainer Rocky Balboa, Apollo's son Adonis Johnson accepts a challenge from Drago's son -- another dangerous fighter. Under guidance from Rocky, Adonis trains for the showdown of his life -- a date with destiny that soon becomes his obsession. Now, Johnson and Balboa must confront their shared legacy as the past comes back to haunt each man.
